check_descriptions.public_requirement: outputs/LuxC.hmm exists, is non-empty UTF-8 text, and starts with the HMMER3/f ASCII profile header line.
check_descriptions.rationale: Baseline presence/encodability control for the first requested artifact before any scientific comparison.

check_descriptions.public_requirement: outputs/LuxC.domtbl exists, is non-empty UTF-8 text, and starts with the three comment header lines of the hmmsearch domain table.
check_descriptions.rationale: Baseline presence/encodability control for the second requested artifact before any scientific comparison.

check_descriptions.public_requirement: The profile header carries the reference model's scientific fields — NAME, ACC, DESC, LENG, ALPH, the annotation flags RF/MM/CONS/CS/MAP, NSEQ, EFFN, CKSUM, GA/TC/NC and the three STATS LOCAL MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD lines (DATE/COM excluded). NAME, ACC, DESC, GA/TC/NC and NSEQ must agree with the alignment's #=GF ID/AC/DE, GA/TC/NC and SQ annotations.
check_descriptions.rationale: Every header field the question names is compared token-level against the reference at its printed precision (exact for integer fields) and simultaneously grounded in the trusted Stockholm #=GF annotations and sequence count via BIOTASKS_TRUSTED_INPUT_DIR, so a wrong accession, cutoff, sequence count, effective sequence number or calibrated local-mode statistic is rejected.

check_descriptions.public_requirement: The calibrated model block — alphabet and transition-order header lines, the COMPO composition line, the null-model insert and transition lines, and for every match state the 20 emission parameters, insert-state emission line, seven transition parameters and the five per-state annotation tokens (`*` for zero-probability parameters), ending with the // terminator — matches the reference profile state by state. Parameter values are compared as the negative natural-log model probabilities the writer serializes, at the reference's printed precision; `*` is a format token compared by identity.
check_descriptions.rationale: State-by-state token comparison at the reference's printed precision: a wrong emission score, insert emission, transition, MAP index or consensus residue inside a structurally intact model is rejected on its value, and a model block whose line count or layout disagrees with its declared LENG is reported as a layout mismatch after the common prefix has been token-compared, so wrong values inside a mis-sized block are never hidden behind the count abort.

check_descriptions.public_requirement: The domain table has the reference's three comment header lines and exactly the reference data rows in the same rank order; each row's 22 fixed fields and the free-text target description match the corresponding reference row, and target names, lengths and descriptions agree with the searched database.
check_descriptions.rationale: Row count, rank order, all 22 fixed fields and the description are compared token-level against the reference (exact integers, half-a-last-place tolerance for printed decimals), with the target name, ungapped length and description grounded in the trusted FASTA header, so invented identifiers, wrong coordinates, wrong scores/E-values and reordering or dropped rows are all rejected.

check_descriptions.public_requirement: The domain table is internally consistent and input-grounded: query name/accession/length equal the profile's NAME/ACC/LENG; hmm coordinates lie within 1..profile length, alignment and envelope coordinates within 1..target length; domain numbers run 1..n per target; rows are ordered by non-increasing full-sequence bit score; and every reported full-sequence E-value is at most the reporting threshold 10.
check_descriptions.rationale: Cross-artifact relations the question requires: the submission's own domain table must cohere with the submission's own profile and with the searched database, and a profile whose model block does not match its declared LENG also fails this check, so the domain table cannot be consistent with a malformed profile.

probe_concerns: Formatting widths remain declared 'provisional' in the instruction while the addendum compares the domtbl in full and the HMM 'line structure (token counts per line type)' writer layout; the valid-representation probe only appends digits within the existing writer layout. The grader compares whitespace-delimited tokens, so identical values in a differently spaced rendering (e.g. a native HMMER CLI writer) still pass token comparison.
The three fixed '#' comment header lines of the domtbl are compared in full while the profile's DATE/COM provenance is excluded; this asymmetry appears deliberate and is retained.

Resolved by this repair: the model-block comparison now token-compares the common prefix of the model block and reports a line-count/layout mismatch only as an additional message, so the recorded hmm-model-block mutation is rejected on its mutated values (wrong emission score, MAP index, consensus residue, insert line) and then on its truncated layout, and hmm_profile_consistency still fails on the layout mismatch. The '*' token-identity path remains exercised by the hmm-terminal-star-to-number probe. Probe scripts, names, focus and citations are unchanged; all scientific checks retain wrong-result coverage.
grader_repair.rationale: Two recorded defects are corrected coherently, with all check identities, kinds and artifact associations preserved. (1) Grader coverage defect: the prior parse_hmm aborted on the model-block line-count branch before any token comparison, so the recorded hmm-model-block mutation's wrong values (state-1 emission 2.07294->2.37294, MAP index 1->2, consensus residue l->m, insert-emission 2.40513->2.90513) were never value-compared; the rejection of a well-formed wrong value in the model body was not demonstrated. The repaired grader parses a mis-sized model block tolerantly, validates every state triple that is present, token-compares the reference/common prefix of the model block (value errors reported first), and appends the layout/count mismatch as an additional message, with domtbl_profile_consistency also reporting it. The unchanged probe script therefore now yields a value-level rejection ('value ... differs from reference ... by more than half a unit in the reference's last printed place') in addition to the layout mismatch. Every prior control outcome is preserved: reference, recomputed and alternative submissions still pass (no mismatch when counts agree); empty, misplaced and missing-file controls still fail identically; the header, star-token, domtbl-value, coordinate and tolerance-boundary probes are unaffected (counts match and parsing succeeds there); the extra-digits valid alternative still parses and passes. (2) Consistency with the corrected public question: the acceptance addendum (preserved unchanged via null) makes no units claim and remains sound; the check descriptions are updated so hmm_model explicitly states the negative natural-log model-probability convention and the value-first comparison of the common prefix. No tolerance was widened, no criterion weakened, and no probe annotation changed: the probe script, name, focus and source citations stay fixed, and all scientific checks retain wrong-result coverage.

instruction:
# Build a profile HMM from a multiple sequence alignment and search a protein database

## Objective

You are given a curated multiple sequence alignment of the LuxC protein family (acyl-CoA reductase, Pfam entry PF05893) in Stockholm format, and a FASTA file of full-length LuxC-family protein sequences. Your job is to reproduce the two terminal products of this analysis:

1. **A profile hidden Markov model (HMM)** built from the alignment, in HMMER ASCII profile format.
2. **A domain-search result table** produced by searching the protein database with that profile HMM, in the tabular domain format that HMMER's `hmmsearch` writes (domain table, one row per reported domain).

## Supplied inputs

- `inputs/data/msa/LuxC.sto` — the multiple sequence alignment in Stockholm 1.0 format. It carries Pfam-family annotations (`#=GF ID`, `#=GF AC`, `#=GF DE`) and scoring cutoff annotations (`#=GF GA`, `#=GF TC`, `#=GF NC`). The alignment's family name, accession, description and annotated GA/TC/NC cutoffs must be carried into the built HMM, exactly as HMMER's model builder does when constructed from an annotated Stockholm alignment.
- `inputs/data/seqs/LuxC.faa` — the protein sequence database to search, in FASTA format (UniProt-style headers).
- A compatible reference environment (Python 3.13, pyhmmer 0.12.3 providing HMMER 3.4 behavior) is available and may be used, but software choice is open: any implementation that produces the scientifically equivalent profile and domain table under the contract below is acceptable.

## Methodology (consequential — must match)

**Model construction.** Build a Plan7 profile HMM from the alignment using standard HMMER3 model construction with default parameters — i.e. the configuration HMMER's `hmmbuild` uses when invoked without options: fast model architecture determination (match columns assigned by residue-occurrence threshold 0.5), relative sequence weighting, effective sequence number estimated by relative entropy, and alphabet-based Dirichlet mixture priors, against the standard non-uniform amino-acid background model.

**Profile search.** Search the sequence database with the built HMM using the default HMMER3 accelerated pipeline — i.e. the configuration of `hmmsearch` without options: MSV/Viterbi/Forward acceleration filters at their default thresholds (permissive 0.02 / 1e-3 / 1e-5), composition-bias filtering and null2 score correction enabled, and reporting/inclusion by **E-value thresholds, not model-specific bit cutoffs**: per-target and per-domain hits reported at E-value ≤ 10, included at E-value ≤ 0.01. The per-target E-value must be computed with the search-space size Z equal to the number of sequences in the searched database, and the per-domain E-value with the number of significant sequences found.

## Required outputs

Write exactly these two files:

### 1. `outputs/LuxC.hmm`

The profile HMM in HMMER3 ASCII profile format (`HMMER3/f`). Requirements:

- Header fields must state the alignment-annotated name, accession, description and GA/TC/NC cutoffs (trusting the input annotations), the model length, the amino-acid alphabet, the annotation flags (RF/MM/CONS/CS/MAP) and the number of aligned sequences produced by the construction.
- The file must contain the calibrated local-mode statistics (MSV/VITERBI/FORWARD), the null-model composition line, and for every match state of the model: the emission probabilities over the 20 amino acids in the fixed order A C D E F G H I K L M N P Q R S T V W Y, the insert-state emission line, and the seven transition probabilities (m->m, m->i, m->d, i->m, i->i, d->m, d->d), together with the per-state consensus residue, consensus match and map annotations, ending with the null-model insertion line.
- Values are the natural units of the format: each model parameter printed in the composition line, the match-state and insert-state emission lines, and the per-state transition lines is the **negative natural-log probability of that model parameter**, written with five decimal places — a parameter probability of exactly zero is written `*` (and one of exactly one as `0.00000`). These are **not** log-odds or background-relative scores: no background division is applied in this file; log-odds relative to the background distribution are formed only later, inside the calibrated Plan7 search profile used for searching.
- The runtime-stamped `DATE` and `COM` lines are provenance only and are **not** part of the compared content; every other field and line is scientific content and must correspond to the reference computation described above.

### 2. `outputs/LuxC.domtbl`

The domain-search results in the tabular domain-table format that `hmmsearch` produces (with `--domtblout`): three comment header lines describing the columns, followed by **one data row per reported domain** — a domain being a single significant match of the profile to one region of one target sequence. Requirements:

- Each data row has the 22 fixed-width fields followed by the free-text target description, in the standard order: target name; target accession ("-"); target length; query name; query accession; query length; full-sequence E-value; full-sequence bit score; full-sequence bias; domain number and total domains for that target; domain c-Evalue and i-Evalue; domain bit score and bias; hmm coordinates (from, to); alignment coordinates (from, to); envelope coordinates (from, to); mean posterior accuracy of the domain alignment; description of target.
- The **target name** is the first whitespace-delimited token of each FASTA header (e.g. a UniProt-style identifier such as `sp|P19841|LUXC_PHOPO`); the description is the remaining text of that header.
- **Row order encodes rank**: rows are ordered by decreasing full-sequence bit score (hmmsearch's canonical ordering); this ordering must be preserved.
- The rows report exactly the domains passing the reporting thresholds of the pipeline described above (all sequences may or may not yield hits — report what the method yields, not an assumed number of rows).
- E-values are reported in the format's scientific notation, and scores in bits, as the format's fixed-precision rendering; these must correspond to the reference computation.

## Constraints

- Offline environment; no network access.
- Reference implementation environment: pyhmmer 0.12.3 (HMMER 3.4), Python 3.13.
- Time limit: 600 seconds. Resources: 4 CPUs, 8 GiB memory.
- Do not modify the supplied input files; the profile must be rebuilt from the alignment, not sourced from any precomputed HMM fixture.
- Numerical comparison tolerances and exact formatting/width conventions are provisional until the executable validation stage; the requested quantities, populations, ordering and field meanings above are the binding scientific contract.
rationale: Diagnosis verified directly against the hash-verified pyhmmer 0.12.3 source and the reference output, not taken from the reviewer's assertions. (1) The public question's units bullet is false: `vendor/hmmer/src/p7_hmmfile.c` (printprob, lines 2091–2097 of the installed release source) writes each HMMER3/f model parameter as `-logf(p)` of that stored probability in plain natural-log units — `*` for p==0, `0.00000` for p==1 — and the writer's callers (lines 576–622) feed `hmm->compo`, `hmm->ins[k][x]`, `hmm->mat[k][x]` and `hmm->t[k][x]` straight to it with no null/background division (contrast the legacy HMM2 `h2_io.c` writer, which did divide match emissions by `bg->f[x]`). The reference file confirms it: node-0 `m->m` `0.01473` = −ln(0.98539), a negative natural-log model probability, not a log-odds score. A correct independent implementation following the original "log odds expressed as negative log probabilities" label would be scientifically misdirected, so the base question must be corrected (public_question target) while the fixed scientific target and acceptance contract stay unchanged. The correction is confined to that single bullet: the values are negative natural-log probabilities of the model parameters, `*` for zero (and `0.00000` for one), not background-relative log-odds; log-odds are formed only later in the calibrated Plan7 search profile. Everything else in the instruction is reproduced verbatim. The independent implementation is otherwise consistent with the public contract (default hmmbuild/hmmsearch configuration, same writers) and needs no independent_issues. (2) The same recorded review identified a genuine grader/probe-coverage defect, so it is corrected in grader_repair rather than frozen: the prior parser aborted on the model-block line-count branch before any token comparison, so the recorded hmm-model-block mutation's wrong values were never value-compared. The repaired grader tolerantly parses a mis-sized block, token-compares the common prefix (value errors reported first), and reports the layout/count mismatch as an additional message (also in domtbl_profile_consistency); unchanged check identities, kinds and artifact associations; the acceptance addendum is preserved unchanged (it makes no units claim); probe scripts, names and citations are fixed and untouched. All previously-passing controls remain valid: reference/recomputed/alternative pass, empty/misplaced/missing fail, all other probes unaffected.
